QUESTION:
Which other drugs interact with Metformin Hydrochloride?

RESPONSE:
Short answer: the excerpt you've given me (Indications and Dosage & Administration sections only) does not contain the Drug Interactions section, so I can't quote specific interaction information from this label. The only interaction-type guidance visible here is about iodinated contrast media:

• Iodinated contrast imaging (Section 2.4): Stop metformin at or before the procedure in patients with an eGFR 30–60 mL/min/1.73 m², in those with a history of liver disease, alcoholism, or heart failure, or in anyone receiving intra-arterial iodinated contrast. Recheck eGFR 48 hours afterward and restart only if renal function is stable. (This is because contrast can cause acute kidney injury, raising the risk of metformin-associated lactic acidosis.)

For completeness, metformin labeling generally describes these interaction categories in Section 7 — please verify against the full prescribing information for this product:

• Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (e.g., topiramate, acetazolamide, zonisamide, dichlorphenamide) – may increase lactic acidosis risk.
• Drugs that reduce metformin clearance via OCT/MATE inhibition (e.g., ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine) – can raise metformin levels and lactic acidosis risk.
• Alcohol – potentiates metformin's effect on lactate metabolism; excessive intake should be avoided.
• Insulin and insulin secretagogues (sulfonylureas, meglitinides) – increased risk of hypoglycemia; lower doses may be needed.
• Drugs that affect glycemic control (e.g., corticosteroids, thiazide and other diuretics, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens/oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, calcium channel blockers, isoniazid) – may cause loss of glycemic control; monitor more closely when starting or stopping them.

Always review the complete label and discuss your full medication list (including over-the-counter drugs and supplements) with your prescriber or pharmacist.
